title: Pullback compatibility of the explicit abelian derived-Hom class map
statement: Let $S,Y,Y\prime$ be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $a:Y\prime\to Y$, $h:Y\to S$, $h\prime:Y\prime\to S$, and $a\gg h=h\prime$. Let $p\in\mathbb N$, let $F,F\prime$ be abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and let $\varphi:a^{-1}F\to F\prime$. Put $A(U)=\mathbb Z[U]$ (free abelian representable followed by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]). For a derived class $z:h^{-1}A(U)[0]\to F[0][p]$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], define $c_h(z)$ by precomposing with the exact-pullback single-functor comparison, taking its derived adjunct [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], applying zeroth homology and its single-functor comparison, applying the canonical shift isomorphism to degree $p$, and evaluating at the identity generator of $A(U)$. Let $b_a(z)$ be the composite of the single of the inverse-image composition comparison, inverse single-functor comparison, derived inverse image of $z$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], shift comparison, and shifted single-functor comparison followed by $\varphi[0]$. Then the canonical higher-direct-image transition $M$ [def-sbc-abelian-higher-direct-image-map] satisfies $M(U)(c_h(z))=c_{h\prime}(b_a(z))$. This is a compatibility of explicitly defined class maps; it asserts neither invertibility nor existence of sheafification isomorphisms.

source.place: Lemma 59.51.7 cohomology comparison, together with Tag 03Q8 canonical sheafification comparison; explicit derived-adjunction coherence elaboration

proof.text: Use the proved abelian single-complex composition equation to rewrite the source comparison. Expand adjuncts abstractly, use naturality of the second unit, naturality of the pullback comparison and first counit, and the first adjunction triangle identity. This proves compatibility with the unshifted derived transition.

Apply shift compatibility of the derived transition, obtaining the equality of shifted adjuncts. Apply zeroth homology and use naturality of its shift isomorphism to rewrite the transition as degree-p homology. Precompose the single-homology comparison and evaluate at the identity generator; composition of sheaf morphisms acts by composition on sections.
